+## Owner-reviewed biometric verification and 1,500-BetaCoins reward release gates
+

+**Approved decision:** the Super Owner personally reviews the submitted evidence and explicitly accepts or rejects it. That human decision alone is sufficient for this product's biometric-verification workflow. Do not require Play Integrity, Apple App Attest, device-bound cryptographic proof, third-party provider attestation, automated face/voice matching, automated classification, or identity-document provider checks as a prerequisite. Do not describe the result as civil identity proof or claim more assurance than the approved manual review provides.
+
+**Required workflow and server safeguards:**
+- [ ] Super Owner-only server authorization with fresh MFA/step-up and immutable audit records for decisions and every private evidence access.
+- [ ] Bind the request and evidence to the canonical authenticated member UID; prevent member self-review, cross-account evidence reuse, forged attempt numbers, and replayed decisions.
+- [ ] Use the pre-established owner-approved spoken phrase/version. The member cannot choose or alter the phrase during submission.
+- [ ] Match the submitted gender value to the member's existing canonical profile value; the verification form cannot override it.
+- [ ] Enforce three total attempts. After a rejection, the next attempt is unavailable until one full calendar month has elapsed. A third rejection closes the verification file permanently; no fourth attempt or extra lockout is allowed.
+- [ ] Enforce biometric voice-evidence duration of at most 20,000 ms and size of at most 5 MiB in capture UI, upload path, server-side byte/container inspection, and tests.
+- [ ] Enforce biometric video duration of 3,000–5,000 ms from uploaded media bytes on the server; client metadata alone is not authoritative.
+- [ ] Keep evidence private, least-privilege, encrypted in transit/at rest as configured, access-audited, and subject to the approved retention/deletion lifecycle. No public URLs or broad owner-media access.
+- [ ] On explicit Super Owner acceptance, atomically activate the server-owned verification status and credit exactly 1,500 BetaCoins through the central economy ledger once per eligible verification lifecycle. Retries/replays must not duplicate the credit.
+- [ ] Renew on one calendar-month boundaries independently of the 90-day email-verification cycle. Expiry/revocation must immediately remove dependent entitlements; do not claw back a legitimately earned reward solely because a later lease expires.
+- [ ] Keep the feature fail-closed until the complete workflow, privacy controls, audit, deletion/retry behavior, and exact-head tests are green.
+
+**Privacy and legal gates remain mandatory:** complete the applicable DPIA/legal review for the actual evidence collected, establish a lawful basis and purpose limitation, provide localized notice and separate consent where required, document retention/deletion/withdrawal/member rights, restrict staff access, and ensure the badge wording accurately describes the manual review. These safeguards do not reintroduce device attestation or automated scoring as approval prerequisites.
 
-**Security status — 14 November 2026:** the previous callable credited 1,500 coins from a client-supplied `localAuthenticationSucceeded` boolean and client attempt ID. This was not server-verifiable proof and could be forged by a modified client. The callable now fails closed with `failed-precondition` and does not write wallet balance, biometric verification status, or reward ledger entries. Regression tests enforce this behavior. Legacy verification records whose method is `local_os_biometric_prompt` or trust model is `client_claim_after_local_os_prompt` are also rejected by biometric entitlement checks, so old client-only claims no longer unlock biometric-gated links. Historical wallet credits are not automatically clawed back: they require a separate ledger audit and owner-approved remediation to avoid debiting legitimate balances. The 1,500-coin reward is intentionally unavailable until a device-bound cryptographic challenge/attestation is verified server-side (fresh nonce, UID/platform/key binding, replay protection, revocation/expiry, and atomic idempotent credit). This is a security containment fix, not completion of biometric verification.
+**Test coverage required on the final candidate:** authorization/MFA, UID and evidence binding, phrase version, immutable gender, attempt boundaries and calendar-month arithmetic, 20-second audio and 3–5-second video byte-level boundaries, malicious/invalid media, private storage access, audit failure fail-closed behavior, concurrent accept/reject, exactly-once wallet credit, replay, expiry/revocation, and deletion retry. Historical CI results are evidence for their own SHAs only; rerun on the final release candidate.

+# Recovery Integration Audit — Domain Branch Inventory (2026-11-22)
+
+## Scope and safety
+- Comparison baseline: `e522acb5a47964b529b84f49bacd9db0167a6dc5`.
+- Working branch: `codex/mawda-recovery-integration-2026-11-21`.
+- This is a read-only source inventory and decision record. No source code was ported in this pass.
+- No merge to the official development branch or `main`, no deployment, and no production/Firebase/billing/retention changes were performed.
+
+## Findings
+
+### Historical unified branches
+- `codex/mawdda-phase1-unified-2026-11-19` compares as 0 ahead / 421 behind the baseline, with `e12897ad7dc5f383501d997117fb1211c67632e7` as merge base. Its integrated history is already carried by the baseline.
+- `codex/mawdda-unified-test-2026-11-18` is divergent (311 ahead / 771 behind; 77 changed paths in the compare response). It is a historical source for review, not a safe whole-branch merge candidate.
+- `codex/mawdda-unified-final` and `codex/mawdda-unified-release` are divergent and show only a small set of unique paths; they are not suitable as replacement baselines without file-level review.
+- `codex/mawdda-unified-final-v2` and `codex/mawdda-unified-final-v3` are behind the selected baseline.
+
+### Economy and store
+- Several economy branches are divergent from the selected baseline, including `codex/economic-phase1-closeout-2026-11-18`, `codex/economic-phase-completion-2026-11-18`, `codex/economy-official-port-2026-11-18`, and `codex/mawdda-economy-selective-port-2026-11-19`.
+- `codex/economy-recovery-2026-11-18` is substantially divergent (618 ahead / 771 behind; 105 changed paths). It must not be merged wholesale.
+- Store hardening branches have small unique deltas (e.g. wallet/store entitlement closure and gift-concurrency regressions). These require semantic comparison against the more recent baseline and current tests before any port.
+- No pricing, quota, or entitlement policy is to be inferred from branch names or historical snapshots.
+
+### Roles, advertising, rooms and calls
+- `codex/phase1-advertising-callable-auth-2026-11-20` compares as behind the baseline; no separate port is indicated by ancestry.
+- The rented-room call-gate branch is divergent (6 ahead / 504 behind) and has four changed paths. Its `room-call-policy.ts` includes call participant/member revalidation helpers; the baseline version also contains these helpers, so this is not yet evidence of a missing feature.
+- Group-call capacity and role-denial branches have small divergent test/source deltas. Inspect their individual commits and current baseline behavior before deciding whether anything is missing.
+
+### Biometric
+- `codex/biometric-final-owner-policy-2026-11-20` compares as behind the baseline.
+- The standalone Super Owner review-state branch has a divergent delta, but `functions/src/biometric-review-state.ts` is byte-identical on that branch and the selected baseline (same blob SHA `f324e85ef69e83f8d180e31cdf5b0fdd67407bbd`). Do not port it.
+- `codex/biometric-server-lifecycle-2026-11-20` is divergent (73 ahead / 421 behind; 23 changed paths). The selected baseline already contains the lifecycle, server wallet-ledger credit, duration limits and integration suite. The specialist branch is not a replacement baseline; compare its remaining tests/docs only for missing assertions.
+- Previously recorded evidence for the selected baseline remains: biometric emulator integration 5 passed / 0 failed, with owner review, versioned consent, exactly-once reward and media-duration rejection covered.
+
+### Media and messaging
+- Media specialist branches are divergent with small commit deltas. Their snapshots of `functions/src/media.ts`, media integration tests and scanner tests are shorter than the selected baseline files. This indicates the branch files are older snapshots, not a safe source to overwrite the baseline with.
+- `codex/mawdda-deep-audit-profile-store` compares as behind the selected baseline.
+- `codex/mawdda-member-inbox-rebased` is divergent with seven changed paths; inspect individual test/index/UI deltas before any port.
+
+## Current decision
+1. Keep `e522acb5` as the integrated recovery baseline.
+2. Do not merge any complete divergent specialist branch.
+3. Prioritize targeted verification of economy/store transaction invariants, role/callable authorization, room/call race regressions, media hold/delete/scanner behavior, and messaging deletion/index behavior.
+4. Port only a demonstrably missing assertion or safe code change, with focused tests and read-back verification.
+5. Re-run the complete Test Center, Flutter analysis/tests/web build, Functions tests, Firestore/Storage emulator suites and security checks on the final candidate SHA.
+6. Treat 5,000-persona simulation, external testing, native release signing/device acceptance and launch readiness as separate gates. None is claimed complete by this inventory.
+
+## Evidence limitation
+Compare endpoints expose branch ancestry and changed-file summaries, not the full semantic effect of every unique commit. This inventory is a triage record, not a claim that every specialist branch has been exhaustively reviewed. Local Termux/Ubuntu historical replay evidence remains incomplete as recorded in the baseline-selection report.
+
+
+## Additional role, capacity and room-media comparisons
+
+- `codex/mawdda-role-capacity-final-2026-11-19` is divergent (40 ahead / 679 behind; 16 changed paths), but its copies of `platform-role-identities.ts`, `platform-role-identities.test.js`, and `advertising-governance.ts` are smaller than the selected baseline. The selected baseline versions are therefore not to be overwritten by this older branch snapshot.
+- The same role-family pattern appears in `codex/mawdda-role-capacity-after-retention-2026-11-19` and `codex/mawdda-step1-role-reconcile-2026-11-19`: divergent histories and several unique docs/tests, but no justification for whole-branch integration.
+- `codex/mawdda-room-audio-duration-enforcement` is divergent (5 ahead / 1,649 behind; 12 changed paths). Its versions of `media.ts` and scanner code are smaller than the selected baseline. Its Flutter room/audio UI files should be reviewed as regression-test references, not copied over current screens without a targeted gap.
+- `codex/mawdda-room-events` is a separate audit-archive concern (4 changed paths: audit archive service, exports, tests and README). It is not the room rental/call lifecycle and must be evaluated independently.
+- `codex/phase1-store-gifting-catalog-version-regressions-2026-11-20` contains a one-file test-only delta in the store-gifting integration suite. Review its exact assertions against the current suite before deciding whether a test-only port is warranted.
+
+## Revised port decision
+The second pass strengthens the decision to retain the selected baseline source files. Several specialist branches contain unique commits but their checked source snapshots are older/smaller than the baseline. The remaining candidate work is primarily assertion-level gap analysis, documentation reconciliation, and checking whether any newer specialist test covers a failure mode not already exercised by the baseline.
+
+
+## Test assertion gap checks completed
+
+- The older media hold/delete branch appeared to add an audit assertion for the scanner object's exact generation. The selected baseline already asserts the same `objectGeneration === generation` condition and additionally requires exactly one matching audit event after an idempotent scanner callback replay. No test port is needed.
+- The older role-capacity branch tests a fixed five-seat boundary for two roles. The selected baseline's role-capacity integration suite is broader: it covers multiple specialist roles, owner-controlled capacity changes and concurrency/oversubscription behavior. The historical branch test is not a missing regression.
+- The older store-gift concurrency and rented-room call-gate test files contain no nonblank source lines absent from the selected baseline test files in the comparison performed. No test port is indicated by those files.
+- The current media implementation writes the scanner verdict's exact object generation into the audit event, matching the baseline integration assertion.
+
+## Outcome of this pass
+No code or test changes were justified by the inspected specialist branches. This is an intentional result: the selected baseline already contains the stronger or equivalent behavior, and importing older snapshots would reduce coverage or risk regressions. Continue with the remaining domains and final candidate validation rather than forcing a merge for its own sake.

+# Mawdda Unified Baseline Selection — 2026-11-22
+
+## Decision
+
+Use `e522acb5a47964b529b84f49bacd9db0167a6dc5` as the current integrated recovery baseline for continued development, while preserving `e12897ad7dc5f383501d997117fb1211c67632e7` as the historical integration-and-CI anchor.
+
+Work only on the side branch `codex/mawda-recovery-integration-2026-11-21` for recovery/integration work. Do not merge to `main`, deploy, change production Firebase resources, enable billing, or change live retention policy.
+
+## Why this is the best-supported chain
+
+1. The historical development archive ref `archive/development-pre-unification-2026-11-15` points to `f068a8b2e3ad`.
+2. The unified integration ref `codex/mawdda-phase1-unified-2026-11-19` points to `e12897ad7dc5f383501d997117fb1211c67632e7`. GitHub ancestry comparison shows this commit is 742 commits ahead of the archive ref and 0 behind it.
+3. The historical anchor `e12897ad` passed two independent GitHub Actions runs:
+   - Run [44792361450](https://github.com/productionhome2022-hash/mawda-platform/actions/runs/44792361450): Flutter analysis/tests/web release build; Cloud Functions compile/unit tests and broad Firestore/Storage emulator suites; scanner image and media sanitization tests. All three jobs succeeded.
+   - Run [44792361211](https://github.com/productionhome2022-hash/mawda-platform/actions/runs/44792361211): retention/room reservation emulator regressions and Flutter UI analysis/widget tests. Both jobs succeeded.
+4. The current development head `e522acb5a47964b529b84f49bacd9db0167a6dc5` is a direct descendant of `e12897ad`: GitHub comparison reports 421 commits ahead and 0 behind, with `e12897ad` as the merge base. Thus the newer branch did not replace the historical integrated tree; it carries that tree forward.
+5. On `e522acb`, GitHub Actions run [44944086740](https://github.com/productionhome2022-hash/mawda-platform/actions/runs/44944086740) succeeded for the complete emulator-only Test Center and Flutter analysis/tests/web release build. Run [44944086768](https://github.com/productionhome2022-hash/mawda-platform/actions/runs/44944086768) also succeeded for economic verification.
+6. The `e522acb` backend log shows the biometric emulator integration suite completed with 5 tests passed and 0 failed. It explicitly passed:
+   - versioned consent and the approved spoken phrase;
+   - ClamAV-approved evidence, Super Owner review and exactly-once reward;
+   - rejection/retry lifecycle;
+   - rejection of out-of-policy audio/video durations.
+7. The current tree contains the server biometric lifecycle, evidence validation, integration tests and the owner review UI route. `lib/screens/super_admin_screen.dart` opens `BiometricReviewScreen`; that screen lists requests, obtains evidence playback, and submits accept/reject decisions. This is stronger evidence of UI wiring than merely finding an unused screen file.
+
+## Biometric constraints confirmed in the current tree
+
+- Audio: maximum 20 seconds and 5 MiB.
+- Video: 3–5 seconds and 25 MiB.
+- Reward: 1,500 BetaCoins, recorded through the server-side wallet ledger and idempotency key.
+- Server-side validation reads MP4 movie/track duration from uploaded bytes, not client-supplied duration metadata.
+- The integration test verifies that acceptance creates the reward once and that repeat acceptance is rejected.
+
+## Why not select the specialist biometric branch as the whole baseline
+
+The branch `codex/biometric-server-lifecycle-2026-11-20` at `f79f146e96b9a4ae1210a1fcc37a861ebebcd294` had a failed PR workflow run [44789805359](https://github.com/productionhome2022-hash/mawda-platform/actions/runs/44789805359). It is useful as a source of changes to inspect, not as the standalone platform baseline. The current `e522acb` tree contains the integrated biometric lifecycle and passed its own emulator test suite.
+
+## Termux/Ubuntu historical-test evidence boundary
+
+The November 21 audit replay script is a new replay, not proof of the original November 16–19 local test run. Its report records dependency/build problems, including a `tsc: not found` result, and must not be described as a successful historical replay. The original local repair sequence and exact local SHA are not fully established by the currently preserved shell-history evidence. GitHub Actions results above are independently verifiable and are not substituted for that missing local evidence.
+
+## Next controlled steps
+
+1. Treat `e522acb` as the recovery integration baseline and `e12897ad` as its historical known-good ancestor.
+2. Inventory code-bearing branches against this baseline by domain (economy/store, roles/Admin Media, profiles, ads, rooms/calls, media/security, biometric).
+3. For each branch, compare source files and tests, then port only changes not already present. Avoid merging whole divergent histories merely because branch names suggest a feature.
+4. Run the relevant focused tests after each port, then the full Test Center and cross-platform checks on the resulting SHA.
+5. Keep unresolved policy questions and production-only operations blocked pending explicit owner approval.
+
+## Scope and non-claims
+
+- This is a baseline selection and evidence record, not a claim of production readiness or a completed 5,000-persona simulation.
+- GitHub Actions success does not prove native iOS/Android device acceptance, release signing, or deployment.
+- No production resources, live data, billing settings, or `main` branch were changed by this selection.
